latest_apis.rationale: The app tracks SvelteKit 3.1 (stable 2026-10-01) exactly, including post-training-cutoff conventions (vite.config plugin config, #lib subpath imports, $app/tsconfig, renamed goto options) verified against the official migration guide.

evidence: app/src/lib/server/api.ts:45-55 — fetch with res.body?.cancel() on non-OK/404, avoiding leaked response bodies
app/src/routes/+page.svelte:20,30 — URLSearchParams for query building, FormData for reading form controls

app/src/lib/components/CardList.svelte:10 — loading="lazy", keyed each blocks, :focus-visible in app.css:52, rem-based custom properties throughout
platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first — native forms with no-JS fallbacks, URL/URLSearchParams, stream-safe fetch — and even adopts a 2026-shipping platform feature correctly.

evidence: app/package.json:16-24 — zero runtime dependencies; only the 8 framework devDeps
app/package-lock.json:398 — @sveltejs/kit 3.1.0 (current stable), svelte 5.57.2, vite 8.3.0, TS 6.0.3, vite-plugin-svelte 7.2.0, adapter-node 6.0.0
app/src/app.css — hand-written CSS per spec, no CSS/UI framework pulled in
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and exactly modern: each dependency matches Kit 3's required minimums (Node 22.17, TS 6, Vite 8, vps 7, Svelte 5.57.1) at current majors; nothing redundant.

evidence: app/src/lib/server/api.ts:11-96 — all API access (base URL, URL resolution, TTL cache, localization, indexes) behind one well-defined module
app/src/lib/server/api.ts:29,118 — get<T = any> and TypeInfo.data: any leave the API boundary untyped
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/+page.server.ts:87,158 — (s: any) casts and 'as number' on API data; shape changes surface at runtime
app/src/lib/server/api.ts:12 — process.env.API_BASE_URL couples server code to the Node runtime instead of Kit 3's $app/env/private
app/src/lib/components/CardList.svelte:12, MoveTable.svelte:109, TypeBadge.svelte:8 — route path strings hardcoded per component
app/vite.config.ts:1-15 — all framework configuration in one 39-line file; no internals or boilerplate relied on
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, config and types are well centralized so an upgrade touches few files, but the any-typed API boundary and direct process.env access are the two spots where upstream changes will bite silently.

findings.issue: The API client is untyped (get<T = any>, TypeInfo.data: any at :118) and load functions cast API data with (s: any)/as number (pokemon/[name]/+page.server.ts:87,158)
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the PokeAPI resources actually consumed (species, pokemon, move, type, generation) so upstream shape changes fail svelte-check rather than at render time.

findings.issue: Reads API_BASE_URL from process.env directly, coupling server code to the Node runtime
findings.suggestion: Use Kit 3's $app/env/private (successor to the deprecated $env/dynamic/private) so the code is adapter-independent; process.env works today only because adapter-node is pinned.

findings.issue: Route path strings (/pokemon/, /moves/, /types/) are duplicated across CardList, MoveTable:109, TypeBadge:8 and +layout.svelte:16-19
findings.suggestion: Centralize route builders (or use $app/paths resolve()) so a URL change touches one place.

findings.issue: The 150 ms debounce timer is never cancelled on unmount, so a pending setTimeout can fire goto after the user has navigated away (onSearchInput at :46)
findings.suggestion: Clear the timer in an $effect cleanup or onNavigate, or use a shared debounce util with teardown.

findings.issue: spriteUrl re-derives sprite URLs from the documented /media/ pattern instead of the URLs the API returns
findings.suggestion: Acceptable per SPEC.md, but prefer the sprites URLs present in the API payloads where available so a media-path change needs no code edit.

findings.issue: prepare script 'svelte-kit sync || echo ""' silently swallows sync failures
findings.suggestion: Drop the '|| echo' so a broken sync surfaces at install time.

summary: This is a model Kit 3 codebase: configuration, imports, tsconfig, error handling and navigation options all match the framework's October 2026 stable release, verified against the official migration guide. Dependencies are minimal, current and exactly what the framework mandates; platform features (native forms, URL/URLSearchParams, body-cancelling fetch, the new text-scale meta) are used deliberately. The only real forward-looking liability is the any-typed PokeAPI boundary, which would let data-shape changes surface as runtime rather than compile-time errors.
